claims.statement: For an arbitrary finite depth alphabet in the aligned ideal all-pair lattice, the scale-alpha count defect has an exact matrix-valued Fourier symbol with two hyperbolic moment channels per spatial frequency.

A q-scale zeroth-order bank has at most 2q channels at each frequency. If M>=2q+2 depth classes, an exact invisible tangent direction exists pointwise. If q<M-1, Q_theta/theta tends to zero along an endpoint-null direction, so no first-order interface coercivity is possible by this symbol mechanism.
For strictly increasing nonnegative scale and depth nodes, the generalized cosh moment matrix has positive determinant, via the even-power expansion and generalized Vandermonde Cauchy-Binet formula.

For a prescribed M-depth alphabet, M-1 distinct aligned scales are necessary and sufficient within this mechanism for a uniform symbol bound Q_theta(z)>=c_* min(theta,1-theta)||z||^2 and hence a nearest-neighbor depth-interface bound. Stationary zero combined defect is a mixture of homogeneous depth phases.

An interval of aligned scales is characteristic for compactly supported depth distributions: a finite signed measure whose cosh scale transform vanishes on an interval is zero. No quantitative finite-scale coercivity follows from this alone.

cannot_imply: The aligned-scale theorem does not establish that actual Zeta23 compressions share one depth-label lattice.
The pointwise null vectors are proof-method obstructions, not physical zeta-zero counterexamples.
No simultaneous small-defect estimate at M-1 source scales has been proved.
No explicit useful lower bound for c_* uniform in a growing alphabet has been proved.
No unconditional zeta-zero proportion is improved.
This checkpoint does not prove or refute the Riemann hypothesis.
